head.h1: Best Catering Companies Dubai: 11 Compared on What They Publish

opening_paragraph: Best Catering Companies Dubai by myCHEF — myCHEF captured 102 per-person prices from six Dubai caterers' own menus in July 2026, and no one company wins on every format. Every competitor figure here was printed on that company's own page or menu PDF, and each carries the link it came from. Medians below are derived from those captured prices and labelled as such.

Those 102 captured lines run from 10 to 570 dirhams a head. Nothing about a competitor on this page is calculated, estimated or inferred. Where a figure is a median, a range or a count, it comes from the capture and is labelled with the number of lines behind it, because a median built on four lines and one built on twenty-two are not the same kind of evidence.

Two disclosures before the numbers, because both change how you should read them. First, myCHEF wrote this guide and myCHEF is one of the eleven catering companies on it. Second, the source-linking claim covers competitor figures only: myCHEF's own rates below are its current rate card, published here, and parts of mychef.ae still carry an older set of figures pending update — so do not treat the myCHEF row as independently checkable the way a linked rival menu PDF is. Naming that is the point; a comparison written by a participant is only worth reading if it says where its own evidence is weaker.

new_paragraphs: These are medians of the captured prices, format by format. They are not a weighted market survey, and the sample limit above applies to every row: 92 of the 102 lines come from two caterers, elements.catering with 57 and tastestudio.ae with 35. Read the n column before you read the median.

Per-format medians derived from the 102 own per-person prices captured from six Dubai caterers, July 2026. Dirhams per head. Format n (captured lines) Range (dirhams) Median of captured prices (dirhams)
Corporate / office buffet lunch 4 15–140 95
Event buffet 22 10–295 132
Canapes / finger food 6 78–180 122
BBQ / grill 17 10–265 100
Live stations 11 25–295 100
Plated / fine dining 6 22–570 370
Breakfast / coffee break 20 15–135 32
All per-person lines combined 102 10–570 78

Do not use the all-in 78 as your comparator. It is dragged down by 20 breakfast and coffee-break lines whose own median is 32 dirhams, so comparing a lunch buffet quote against it is not like-for-like. Take the row that matches your format instead. If you are pricing an office lunch, 95 dirhams is the number — while noting it rests on n=4, of which three are Taste Studio's corporate buffet lunch tiers at 80, 110 and 140. That is a thin base and this page will not dress it up as more.

Where myCHEF lands against those medians, stated plainly. Like-for-like, myCHEF's AED 90 volume entry sits just below the corporate and office buffet lunch median of 95 dirhams (n=4). On plated service the picture reverses: AED 700 to AED 950 per head is roughly twice the plated median of 370 dirhams (n=6), and Elements Catering prints the lowest plated rate in the set at 285 dirhams for three courses; Monchef's 370 dirhams is the lowest that includes the team who cook, serve and clear. Against that 285 floor, myCHEF's AED 700 to AED 950 is 2.5 to 3.3 times the cheapest printed plated rate. If lowest published plated price is your only criterion, that is Elements, not myCHEF.
Format is the honest way to read this list. A caterer strong at office lunch boxes can be the wrong booking for a plated wedding dinner, so match your format first and the shortlist writes itself.
Elements Catering — the deepest published rate card, plated up to 570

Elements publishes more of its own per-head pricing than anyone else here: 57 captured lines running from 10 to 570 dirhams. Plated sit-down dinners run 285 for three courses, 380 for four and 570 for six. Canape packages run 78, 104 and 130 by piece count. Live stations — sushi, taqueria and robata — are priced in guest bands from 30 to 150 pax on its live station menu and robata menu . Not everything it publishes is per head: the 5,000-dirham figure attached to the live carvery station is a minimum spend per event, and staff are booked separately in 4-hour blocks on its staff rates page . Minimums are stated plainly on every menu page: 10 guests site-wide, 20 for buffet with 7 days' notice. Its homepage carries luxury client logos plus Formula 1 Abu Dhabi and EXPO 2020 credits.
Taste Studio — the corporate catering companies benchmark

Taste Studio publishes the most corporate pricing of anyone here: 35 captured per-head lines from 10 to 225 dirhams. Corporate buffet lunch runs 80, 110 and 140 per person, which is the single most useful reference point on this page for anyone buying an office lunch. Staffed finger food runs 115, 150 and 180. Coffee breaks are printed at 40 and 45 on its coffee break PDF . Business-lunch delivery starts at 10 people on its business lunch page , and it states it serves corporate events from 20 to 2,000 people. Booking terms are printed on every package PDF: 100% advance payment, and a cancellation ladder paying back an 80% credit note beyond 72 hours and nothing inside 24 hours. Its about page displays an HACCP certification mark and states a halal-certified kitchen, trading from 2015.
Al Safadi — Lebanese buffet at a printed rate, with a 30-person floor

Al Safadi prints four per-head rates in one catering menu PDF: buffet set menus at 200, 230 and 265 per person, and a breakfast buffet at 135. The terms carry the strictest published headcount in this group — 30 persons minimum on every buffet package, and 12 pieces minimum per canape item. Orders need 3 to 5 days depending on size, with a 50% deposit and full settlement 24 hours before, all printed in the same menu PDF . The restaurant group trades from 2000 on its story page and names its executive chef in the menu. If you want Lebanese food for 30 or more at a rate you can read before you call, this is the clearest option in this comparison.
myCHEF — two bands printed, mid-market on volume, premium on plated

MyCHEF prices two bands and prints both. Volume formats start at AED 90 per head for a working office lunch, AED 120 for a standard event buffet, and AED 150 for premium buffet, BBQ, live stations or canapes. A chef cooking, plating and serving on site is AED 700 to AED 950 per head. Minimums are 10 guests for volume formats, 20 for a full buffet, and AED 900 minimum order value. Against the per-format medians on this page, that puts the AED 90 entry just below the 95-dirham corporate lunch median and the plated band at roughly twice the 370-dirham plated median. One caveat belongs here, not in small print: these rates are published in this guide and quoted on enquiry, and parts of mychef.ae still show an older set of figures that are being updated, so they are not yet cross-checkable across our own site the way a rival's linked menu PDF is. MyCHEF designs and manages each experience; appropriately licensed culinary partners perform the regulated food services. See the full catering price list or the catering packages .
Buffestra — banded BBQ pricing with staff included

Buffestra prices BBQ in three own tiers on one package card: 90 to 140 per person for the BBQ buffet, 140 to 210 for the live grill station it flags as most popular, and 210 and up for the premium grill feast. Chafing setup and staff sit inside those figures, which is unusual at that level. Worth knowing before you quote its site back at anyone: most of the price ranges on Buffestra's pages are editorial market estimates for Dubai catering generally, not Buffestra's own rates, and only the three package-card bands are its own. No minimum headcount or order value appears anywhere. Its homepage states 500+ events catered and trading from 2013, and the BBQ page describes the company as "Dubai Municipality compliant, certificate on request" instead of displaying the certificate.
Monchef — the lowest printed plated rate that includes service, six guests minimum

Monchef prints one rate: 370 dirhams plus VAT per person for a seven-course silver-service private dining experience, minimum 6 pax and maximum 20 through online booking. The team arrives about an hour before service with equipment and ingredients, cooks, serves and clears the kitchen, and the same offer appears on its homepage . Every other format on the site, including corporate catering , BBQ, canapes and outdoor catering, ends in a contact form with no figure. For a small plated dinner at a published rate, Monchef is the cheapest printed option in this comparison, and by a wide margin — including against myCHEF.
Dish — luxury brand events, one printed rate

Dish positions around brand and celebrity events and its proof follows that: a client logo wall on its homepage including BCG, DHL, Cartier, Rolex and BMW, a stated Catering Company of the Year title at the Leaders in F and B Awards 2024, trading from 2008 on its about page , and a stated team of 200+. One own rate appears in its published writing: 295 per person for Ramadan iftar catering. Its private dining menu starts at 20 guests, and it states a ratio of one server per 10 guests for a luxury sit-down meal. Tenure figures differ between its own pages — 18 years on its corporate page against over 15 years on the homepage. That is worth a question, not a conclusion.
Smart Catering — office boxes priced per package, 6 hours' notice

Smart Catering is the one company here you can order from like a shop: 43 published prices, an online checkout, and orders accepted 6 hours before delivery within 9am to 9pm on its homepage . Every one of those prices is per package, not per head, which is why none of them enters the per-person medians on this page. Its largest listed package, office catering for 20 , serves 10 to 20 people and lists at 1,380 dirhams for the package. Delivery is free over 1,000 dirhams in Dubai on its delivery page . It states no minimum headcount or order value, carries no founding year, no client logos and no compliance badge, and its reviews page displays no reviews. For a last-minute office order at a known total, that trade-off may still suit you.
HFE — per-item shop pricing and an inconsistent notice period

HFE publishes 7 prices, all attached to shop products sold per item: bites, salads, breakfast, cake, sweet bites and cold-pressed juice. Because they are per item and not per head, they are excluded from the medians on this page. Each product page asks for orders at least 48 hours in advance, while HFE's own house-party page claims a 3-hour turnaround, its corporate page asks 2 to 4 weeks for large events and its events page states 7 days. Four different notice periods on one site is exactly the red flag described further down. No minimum headcount, order value or delivery fee appears anywhere, and no client logos, review counts or compliance badges show on the pages read, so its case rests on chef credentials and its menu PDF.
Cedar Tree Catering — the fullest credential stack, no own rate card

Across the 205 Dubai catering searches captured for this guide, Cedar Tree appeared in the top three more often than any other company here, and its strength is proof, not price. Its about page states HACCP and ISO 22000:2018, its homepage displays a Dubai Municipality Approved seal and an SGS badge, and its client carousel carries 20+ enterprise logos including Sony, Samsung, Amazon and Accenture. It trades from 2007. Its site-wide terms, repeated on its menu page and Click and Eat page , set a minimum order value of 700 dirhams excluding 5% VAT, a minimum of one dozen per item, and Click and Eat orders placed 1 day ahead. For its own services it prints no per-head rate anywhere. Its cost blog quotes a Dubai market range of 80 to 500 dirhams per person, which describes the market, not Cedar Tree.
Baguette — institutional scale, no published rate

Baguette runs at a scale nobody else here matches: 700 employees across 48 nationalities and 10,000 meals a day, trading from 2004, with Dubai Municipality approval and ADPHC-Sehhi programme certification stated on its catering page , plus government and airline client logos. It publishes no per-head rate, no minimum headcount and no minimum order value. Its lead-time guidance differs between its own pages, from 1 to 2 weeks on that catering page to 4 to 6 weeks on its wedding catering page . For contract volume feeding, that scale matters more than a printed rate does.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: Red flags with catering companies, and the six questions to ask
replace_in_block.new_heading: Red flags with catering companies, and the six questions to ask
new_paragraphs: A red flag is not proof of a bad caterer. It is a signal that one question needs an answer before you pay a deposit. These six do most of the work, and each one came out of the sites read for this guide.

Ask: what guest count does this per-head rate assume? A rate with no headcount behind it moves once the real number lands. Elements Catering prices live stations in bands from 30 to 150 pax for exactly that reason. A weak answer: "it depends on the event." A workable answer: "that figure holds from 40 guests; below that it moves, and here is the new number."

Ask: is staffing inside the figure or beside it? Buffestra prints staff and chafing setup inside its 90-to-140 BBQ band; Elements Catering books staff separately in 4-hour blocks. Both are honest. A quote that hides which one it is becomes a second invoice. A weak answer: "everything is included." A workable answer: a line item.

Ask: what is your minimum, in writing, today? Minimums here run from 6 pax to 30 persons, and four of the eleven publish none. A weak answer: "let's discuss it on a call." A workable answer: a number in an email, before you spend time on a call.

Ask: which document sits behind that compliance claim? Buffestra states "certificate on request"; Cedar Tree Catering displays its seals on the page. A weak answer: a badge image with no issuing body and no date. A workable answer: the issuer, the activity it covers, and an offer to show it.

Ask: what notice do you need for my exact format? Published notice in this set runs from 6 hours at Smart Catering to 4 to 6 weeks for a Baguette wedding, and HFE's own pages give four different answers. A weak answer: a number that changes when you push. A workable answer: a lead time tied to your format and headcount.

Ask: how does the kitchen doing my cooking handle allergens? Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event. A weak answer: a blanket safety promise. A workable answer: what the kitchen can and cannot control.

One more flag deserves naming because it is the commonest and least discussed: a market-average price quoted at you by a company that publishes no rate of its own tells you what other people charge, not what you will pay. Cedar Tree's cost blog is the clearest instance in this set — an 80 to 500 dirham range, with no own figure on any service page. Buffestra's pages carry the same pattern in a milder form, where editorial ranges outnumber its own three package bands.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: How to choose a caterer in Dubai, in five moves
replace_in_block.new_heading: How to choose a caterer in Dubai, in five moves
new_paragraphs: Choosing well is a process, not a hunch. Five moves get you a decision you can defend to whoever signs the invoice.

Pick the format before the company. Drop-off, buffet, live station, plated. Format sets the floor: the captured medians run from 32 dirhams for a coffee break to 370 for plated dining, a spread no menu choice will close.

Send one identical brief to three caterers. Same date, same guest count, same venue, same dietary list. Different briefs produce quotes that cannot be compared, which is how buyers end up choosing on presentation.
Check the minimum before the menu. A 30-person floor kills a 20-person party whatever the food looks like, and four companies here publish no minimum at all — so you have to ask.
Get food, staffing, equipment, delivery and 5% VAT on separate lines. One blended number cannot be compared against anything, including the medians on this page.
Verify the compliance claim that matters for your venue. Villa, yacht, office and public venue each carry different requirements under the Dubai Municipality Food Safety Department .
Run the cost calculator or read how to choose a caterer in Dubai if you want the arithmetic done before the calls start.

replace_in_block.block_on_your_page: The question no rate card on this page answers: will that live station run at your venue?
replace_in_block.new_heading: The question no rate card on this page answers: will that live station run at your venue?
new_paragraphs: Eleven companies price live stations. None of them says where the station is allowed to be lit, and in Dubai that is the constraint that cancels menus after the deposit has been paid. A robata counter is an open charcoal fire with guests standing at it, so it belongs on a villa's own plot — garden, driveway or ground-level pool deck — and Dubai Municipality's barbecue guidance settles the indoor half of the question in one line: "Do not light coal in an enclosed space or indoors." On an apartment balcony it is refused outright, because Emaar's vertical-community rules prohibit "barbecues, grills, or any cooking equipment of any kind" on balconies and terraces regardless of fuel. On a yacht it is refused for a different reason again: no extra gas cylinder may be brought aboard under D‑Marin's marina regulations (Art. 53.1(a)), and live fire alongside is banned. Where charcoal is out, myCHEF runs the identical skewer card on an electric or induction robata counter, or pre-chars over charcoal in a licensed partner kitchen and finishes the skewers on the counter in front of guests. For a rooftop or a desert site, myCHEF confirms the setup with the building management or the site operator before quoting it, rather than printing a promise here.

Live carvery is the opposite case, and it is why it sits on almost every myCHEF quote: no flame, no fuel, no extraction to arrange, so it runs at a villa, at a permitted beach event, in an apartment and on a yacht deck alike, with only food-safety hot-holding to manage. That is also what makes it the substitute whenever something fired is refused — a shawarma cone cooked in a licensed partner kitchen, carried hot-held on its skewer and carved live on deck gives guests the same shaved-to-order ritual, with the fire two hours earlier and on land. Put the question to every caterer you shortlist, ours included: at my venue, under my building's rules, what actually lights — and what runs instead if it does not?

replace_in_block.new_heading: Where myCHEF is not the right booking
new_paragraphs: A comparison that ends "we win everything" is worth nothing, so here is the straight version, in the same dirhams and the same medians used everywhere else on this page.

On plated dining, myCHEF is expensive. AED 700 to AED 950 per head is roughly twice the plated median of 370 dirhams (n=6). Monchef prints 370 dirhams for seven silver-service courses with a team that cooks, serves and clears — the lowest printed plated rate that includes service. Elements Catering prints the lowest plated rate outright at 285 for three courses, rising to 380 for four and 570 for six, with staff and equipment charged separately. If a plated dinner at the lowest published rate is your priority, book Monchef; the number says so and no amount of positioning changes it.

On volume formats, myCHEF is mid-market, not cheap. The AED 90 entry sits just below the 95-dirham corporate lunch median from four captured lines, and above Taste Studio's 80-dirham entry tier. For a 200-person Lebanese buffet, Al Safadi's printed 200 per person comes from a restaurant group that does exactly that and nothing else. For a same-day office order, Smart Catering accepts orders 6 hours ahead and myCHEF does not. For contract-scale daily feeding, Baguette's 10,000 meals a day is a different business from ours.

Where myCHEF earns a booking is a different axis: both price bands published instead of one, a single accountable team on one brief and one itemised quote, and a culinary partner matched to your cuisine instead of one house menu stretched across every event. That is a genuine trade and you are entitled to value it differently.
What is the leading catering company in Dubai?

There is no single leader across every format, and a page that names one without a test is guessing. On published per-person pricing, Elements Catering leads: 57 of the 102 own per-person prices captured in July 2026 are its own, spanning 10 to 570 dirhams. Taste Studio is second with 35 lines, 10 to 225 dirhams. On displayed compliance credentials, Cedar Tree Catering shows the fullest stack, including a Dubai Municipality Approved seal plus HACCP and ISO 22000:2018 on its about page, while publishing no rate of its own. On plated dining at a printed price, Monchef is the cheapest printed option in the set at 370 dirhams per person for seven-course silver service. Choose by format, not by rank.
What are the top 10 catering companies in Dubai?

This guide compares ten Dubai caterers plus myCHEF: Elements Catering, Taste Studio, Al Safadi, Buffestra, Monchef, Dish, Smart Catering, HFE, Cedar Tree Catering and Baguette. They were selected by how often they appeared in the top three across 205 harvested Dubai catering searches in July 2026, not by paying for a slot. Six of the ten print their own per-person rates. Two print per-package or per-item prices only. Two print no price of their own at all.
How much do catering companies in Dubai charge per person?

It depends on format, so use a per-format figure, not one market number. Across 102 own per-person prices captured from six Dubai caterers' own sites and menu PDFs in July 2026, the medians of those captured prices were: corporate or office buffet lunch 95 dirhams (n=4, range 15 to 140); event buffet 132 dirhams (n=22, range 10 to 295); canapes or finger food 122 dirhams (n=6, range 78 to 180); BBQ or grill 100 dirhams (n=17, range 10 to 265); live stations 100 dirhams (n=11, range 25 to 295); plated or fine dining 370 dirhams (n=6, range 22 to 570); breakfast or coffee break 32 dirhams (n=20, range 15 to 135). The all-in median across all 102 lines is 78 dirhams, but it is dragged down by the 20 breakfast and coffee-break lines with a median of 32, so it is not a like-for-like comparator for a lunch buffet. Read every figure with its limit: 92 of the 102 lines come from two caterers, elements.catering with 57 and tastestudio.ae with 35, so this describes two menus far more than it describes the Dubai market.
Is myCHEF the cheapest catering company in Dubai?

No. Like-for-like, myCHEF's AED 90 volume entry sits just below the corporate and office buffet lunch median of 95 dirhams, and that median rests on only four captured lines. On plated service myCHEF is the premium end of this set: AED 700 to AED 950 per head is roughly twice the plated median of 370 dirhams from six captured lines, and Elements Catering prints the lowest plated rate at 285 dirhams for three courses, and Monchef's 370 dirhams is the lowest including the service team. If the lowest printed price is your only criterion, Elements is the better plated booking, and Taste Studio's 80-dirham corporate buffet lunch is the better office lunch.
Which Dubai catering companies publish their prices?

Six of the ten competitors here print their own per-person rates: Elements Catering with 57 captured lines, Taste Studio with 35, Al Safadi with 4, Buffestra with 3, Monchef with 2 and Dish with 1. Smart Catering and HFE do publish prices, but per package and per item, not per head. Cedar Tree Catering and Baguette publish no own rate at all and quote on request. Cedar Tree does run a cost blog quoting a Dubai market range of 80 to 500 dirhams per person, which is a claim about the market, not its own rate card.
What minimum order do Dubai catering companies require?

Minimums vary by a factor of five and catch more buyers than price does. Al Safadi states 30 persons on every buffet package. Elements Catering states 10 guests site-wide, 20 for buffet, plus a 5,000-dirham minimum spend on its live carvery station. Taste Studio states 10 people for business-lunch delivery and takes corporate events from 20 to 2,000. Dish states 20 guests for its private dining menu. Monchef states 6 pax. Cedar Tree Catering publishes no headcount minimum but sets a minimum order value of 700 dirhams excluding 5% VAT. Buffestra, Baguette, HFE and Smart Catering publish none. MyCHEF applies 10 guests for volume formats, 20 for a full buffet, and a minimum order value of AED 900.
What are common red flags with catering companies?

Six recur across the sites read for this guide. A per-head rate quoted with no guest count behind it. Staffing buried inside a blended figure with no line item. A minimum that will not be put in writing before a call. A compliance claim with no issuing body or date behind it. A lead time that differs between pages of the same website, which happens on more than one site in this comparison. And a market-average price quoted at you by a company that publishes no rate of its own. None of these proves bad catering on its own. Each one tells you which question to ask next.
How do I choose a caterer in Dubai?

Fix the format first, because format sets the floor far more than the menu does: the captured medians run from 32 dirhams for a coffee break to 370 dirhams for plated dining. Then send one identical brief to three caterers, with date, guest count, venue, service style and dietary needs. Ask each for food, staffing, equipment, delivery and 5% VAT on separate lines. Check the minimum before the menu, because a 30-person floor kills a 20-person party whatever the food looks like. Compare per head on one identical headcount, with every quote on the same side of the tax line.
Do Dubai caterers include VAT in the per-head price?

Mostly no. Monchef prints its rate as 370 dirhams plus VAT per person. Cedar Tree Catering states its minimum order value as 700 dirhams excluding 5% VAT. Catering and restaurant services in the UAE carry 5% VAT, in force since 1 January 2018 per the UAE Ministry of Finance. Every myCHEF figure on this page is pre-VAT too. Put every quote on the same side of the tax line before you compare.

Every competitor figure on this page came off that company's own website or menu PDF between 26 and 31 July 2026, recorded word for word with its URL. No competitor figure is calculated, estimated or inferred, and none comes from a directory, an aggregator or a review site. The ten competitors were selected by how often they appeared in the top three across 205 harvested Dubai catering searches; myCHEF appears because myCHEF wrote the page, not because it ranked.

How the aggregates were computed, and what was corrected. The 102 lines are per-person rates a company publishes for its own services. Editorial "cost of catering in Dubai" ranges were excluded, because a market estimate on a caterer's blog is not that caterer's price — that exclusion alone removes 15 lines from Buffestra's site. Per-package and per-item prices (Smart Catering, HFE) are shown in the table but excluded from the per-person medians, since mixing them in would compare different units. Every median and range on this page is derived from the captured prices and labelled as such, and the sample concentration is restated wherever an aggregate appears: 92 of the 102 lines come from two caterers, elements.catering with 57 and tastestudio.ae with 35. An earlier version of this page published a distribution filtered to a floor of 40 dirhams, which discarded 43% of the captured lines — every one of them a cheap line — and reported a median 67% higher than the true one. That version is withdrawn and the figures here are computed on the unfiltered capture.

faq.question: What is the leading catering company in Dubai?
answer: There is no single leader across every format, and a page that names one without a test is guessing. On published per-person pricing, Elements Catering leads: 57 of the 102 own per-person prices captured in July 2026 are its own, spanning 10 to 570 dirhams. Taste Studio is second with 35 lines, 10 to 225 dirhams. On displayed compliance credentials, Cedar Tree Catering shows the fullest stack, including a Dubai Municipality Approved seal plus HACCP and ISO 22000:2018 on its about page, while publishing no rate of its own. On plated dining at a printed price, Monchef is the cheapest printed option in the set at 370 dirhams per person for seven-course silver service. Choose by format, not by rank.

faq.question: What are the top 10 catering companies in Dubai?
answer: This guide compares ten Dubai caterers plus myCHEF: Elements Catering, Taste Studio, Al Safadi, Buffestra, Monchef, Dish, Smart Catering, HFE, Cedar Tree Catering and Baguette. They were selected by how often they appeared in the top three across 205 harvested Dubai catering searches in July 2026, not by paying for a slot. Six of the ten print their own per-person rates. Two print per-package or per-item prices only. Two print no price of their own at all.

faq.question: How much do catering companies in Dubai charge per person?
answer: It depends on format, so use a per-format figure, not one market number. Across 102 own per-person prices captured from six Dubai caterers' own sites and menu PDFs in July 2026, the medians of those captured prices were: corporate or office buffet lunch 95 dirhams (n=4, range 15 to 140); event buffet 132 dirhams (n=22, range 10 to 295); canapes or finger food 122 dirhams (n=6, range 78 to 180); BBQ or grill 100 dirhams (n=17, range 10 to 265); live stations 100 dirhams (n=11, range 25 to 295); plated or fine dining 370 dirhams (n=6, range 22 to 570); breakfast or coffee break 32 dirhams (n=20, range 15 to 135). The all-in median across all 102 lines is 78 dirhams, but it is dragged down by the 20 breakfast and coffee-break lines with a median of 32, so it is not a like-for-like comparator for a lunch buffet. Read every figure with its limit: 92 of the 102 lines come from two caterers, elements.catering with 57 and tastestudio.ae with 35, so this describes two menus far more than it describes the Dubai market.

faq.question: Is myCHEF the cheapest catering company in Dubai?
answer: No. Like-for-like, myCHEF's AED 90 volume entry sits just below the corporate and office buffet lunch median of 95 dirhams, and that median rests on only four captured lines. On plated service myCHEF is the premium end of this set: AED 700 to AED 950 per head is roughly twice the plated median of 370 dirhams from six captured lines, and Elements Catering prints the lowest plated rate at 285 dirhams for three courses, and Monchef's 370 dirhams is the lowest including the service team. If the lowest printed price is your only criterion, Elements is the better plated booking, and Taste Studio's 80-dirham corporate buffet lunch is the better office lunch.

faq.question: Which Dubai catering companies publish their prices?
answer: Six of the ten competitors here print their own per-person rates: Elements Catering with 57 captured lines, Taste Studio with 35, Al Safadi with 4, Buffestra with 3, Monchef with 2 and Dish with 1. Smart Catering and HFE do publish prices, but per package and per item, not per head. Cedar Tree Catering and Baguette publish no own rate at all and quote on request. Cedar Tree does run a cost blog quoting a Dubai market range of 80 to 500 dirhams per person, which is a claim about the market, not its own rate card.

faq.question: What minimum order do Dubai catering companies require?
answer: Minimums vary by a factor of five and catch more buyers than price does. Al Safadi states 30 persons on every buffet package. Elements Catering states 10 guests site-wide, 20 for buffet, plus a 5,000-dirham minimum spend on its live carvery station. Taste Studio states 10 people for business-lunch delivery and takes corporate events from 20 to 2,000. Dish states 20 guests for its private dining menu. Monchef states 6 pax. Cedar Tree Catering publishes no headcount minimum but sets a minimum order value of 700 dirhams excluding 5% VAT. Buffestra, Baguette, HFE and Smart Catering publish none. MyCHEF applies 10 guests for volume formats, 20 for a full buffet, and a minimum order value of AED 900.
